src/utils/transactionReconciliation.ts.note: The mark/commit predicate, and the twin of transactionReview.ts beside it. Three-valued and deliberately so: reconciled true or false is authoritative, and NULL/undefined means the row predates the split and its is_cleared answers — which is how a fifty-thousand row history reads correctly on the day the flag ships. The rule is owned by supabase/migrations/20260810200000_marking_is_not_reconciling.sql; port the two together. reconciledAfterMarking is the other half (marking keeps a commitment, unmarking clears it) and is what stops a store holding the pair reconciled-but-unmarked, which would put the cleared balance and the reconciled set permanently out of step. No is_reconciled column in the local core yet.

src/utils/transactionReview.ts.note: The review-state twin of categoryProvenance.ts beside it, and pending for the same reason: a pure predicate over one boolean whose rule is owned by supabase/migrations/20260810090000_imported_rows_arrive_new.sql, with no needs_review verb in the local core yet. Port it in the same change that ports that migration. The asymmetry IS the whole of it — needsReview === true means new; false, undefined and absent all mean reviewed — and getting it backwards prints every row of history in bold.

src/utils/csvMappingPrefill.ts.note: Which of a saved set of column names apply to the file in hand, for the CSV wizard's template and profile prefill. Sits beside enhancedCsvImportService.ts, which is itself pending: the same import path, the same disposition.

V8 non-standard fallback parsing is deliberately not ported and admission-specs/dedupe-a-date-only-the-browser-can-read-* pins the difference from both sides. normalizeTransactionDates is a read-path helper with no admission decision in it.

src/utils/transferCounterpartOrigin.ts.note: Can this counterpart be PROVED to be scaffolding the app created, so a re-point may move it without asking? One-way by construction: it proves 'the app made this' from createdAt == updatedAt on a LINKED row (only create_transfer_counterpart and the split-leg counterpart insert write a link at INSERT time; every other path links with an UPDATE, and update_transactions_updated_at is a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on the whole table), and it can never prove the opposite. The local edition needs the same rule and the same direction of error, and it needs the same three defence-in-depth signals (is_cleared, statement_sequence, needs_review) because they are what would catch a future inserter that wrote a link alongside real provenance.

src/utils/transferRepoint.ts.note: The crossover rule a linked pair is filed by — EACH SIDE'S To/From CATEGORY NAMES THE OTHER ACCOUNT — written once so repoint_transfer (SQL) and DataService's browser mirror cannot drift. Both categories are DERIVED from the pairing as it will be rather than patched, because the editor can move the row's own account in the same save and then the counterpart's category is stale too. A local port must derive them the same way; getting it backwards files a row under the transfer category of the account it sits in, which is the self-transfer shape isSelfTransferCategory exists to refuse.

src/utils/transferCoherence.ts.note: THE RULE: a transfer CATEGORY and a transfer TYPE must never disagree, on any writing path. Every report classifies by category (classifyFlow), so a row typed income/expense but filed under a To/From category is treated as a transfer everywhere it is counted — out of income, out of spending, out of the uncategorised review band — while the balance still moves and no counterpart exists to answer for it. A local port needs the same predicate at every writer it grows (quick add, the editors, bulk filing, importers) and the same measure for rows already in that state; findMismatchedTransferFilings deliberately reads STORED transactions, never split-expanded rows, because a transfer LEG inside a split is legitimate and the expansion gives every line an income/expense type from its sign.

Splits Money's two states apart: transactions.is_reconciled (nullable, no backfill, so history keeps NULL and its is_cleared answers) and accounts.last_reconciled_balance. Four rules for a local port: set_transactions_cleared keeps a commitment when marking and clears it when unmarking; finalize_reconciliation commits ONLY rows whose is_reconciled is explicitly false and records the day and the ending balance in the same transaction (zero is a balance, absent is not); archive_transactions_before judges COALESCE(is_reconciled, is_cleared); and the archive sweep trigger fires on is_reconciled, never on the mark. scripts/local-sqlite/schema.sql does not carry either column yet.
